label: Underemployment rate
description: The percentage of the labour force who are employed but working fewer hours than they want and are available to work more. A more complete measure of labour market slack than unemployment alone.
explainer: Underemployment captures workers who have a job but cannot get enough hours. A retail worker on 10 hours who wants 38 hours counts as underemployed but not unemployed. The combined unemployment plus underemployment rate rarely falls below 12% even in boom times. It peaked at nearly 15% during Covid. This explains why wage growth was muted for so long despite record-low unemployment — there was more slack in the labour market than the headline rate suggested.
projection_source: RBA Statement on Monetary Policy labour market projections. Underemployment expected to remain above 6% as casual work persists.
notes: ABS seasonally adjusted series. Available from 1978.
